topic_title: Understand and use linear regression models

mission.display_title: Distinguish simple and multiple linear models
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to place the simple vs multiple linear regression forms so you can write the model equation with one or several explanatory variables — without leaping to least-squares algebra yet.
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will force the candidate to write η forms for simple and multiple LM and refuse treating 'multiple' as automatic excellence.
mission.educational_intent: Produce discrimination between single-X and multi-X linear model statements.
mission.learning_objective: State the simple regression model (single explanatory variable) and the multiple linear regression model (several explanatory variables).
mission.concept_focus: One X → several X → write model → refuse multiple-as-better theatre.
mission.prior_bridge: Yesterday you named response and explanatory roles (4.1.1). Today forms the model statement.
mission.why_now: 4.1.2 is contiguous after roles; estimation (4.1.3) needs a stated model.
mission.expected_benefit: Study Progress for model forms — not least squares mastery.
mission.explainability: Campaign Delta Day 2 continues Trust Front at LO 4.1.2.
success_criteria: Closed-book, write the simple LM equation with one X.
Write a multiple LM with at least two X's.
Refuse: 'multiple always beats simple' without criterion.
task_descriptions: Sketch simple vs multiple equations before CMP.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.1.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Write (1) a simple LM for Y on X1; (2) a multiple LM for Y on X1 and X2. Use β notation.
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Simple: Y = β0 + β1 X1 + ε. Multiple: Y = β0 + β1 X1 + β2 X2 + ε (or equivalent).
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.1.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Why is 'always use multiple regression' not a modelling warrant? Give one honest criterion that would justify adding a second X.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Multiple is not automatically better. Add X2 when theory or evidence shows incremental explanatory value (and you will later check fit/residuals) — not by habit.
